column3: I-Chiun eyes Nvidia Vera Rubin supply chain as thermal business nears half of sales
column4: I-Chiun Precision Industry is accelerating its shift from LED lead frames into high-end thermal solutions, with thermal products now accounting for 40-45% of revenue. The company expects the share to exceed 50% as early as the second half of 2026 or in 2027 and to rise above 60% over the medium to long term.

column3: TEL sees AI-driven packaging, memory demand reshaping Taiwan strategy
column4: Tokyo Electron's Taiwan president said AI is pushing semiconductor demand into new areas, with advanced packaging, DRAM, high-bandwidth memory, and NAND flash all gaining momentum. He said Taiwan remains central to the industry's supply chain, and TEL plans to deepen local technology, service, and research ties.

column3: Hanmi's 2.5D bonders pass Taiwan foundry qualification as packaging outsourcing expands
column4: South Korea's Hanmi Semiconductor has reportedly begun supplying 2.5D packaging bonders to an unnamed Taiwanese foundry after the equipment passed mass-production qualification, giving the company an important production foothold as Taiwan's advanced-packaging supply chain expands beyond foundry-owned lines.

column3: Commentary: The pushback against AI songs is music to my ears
column4: For Bloomberg Opinion's Dave Lee, music generated entirely by AI is an abomination and finding it placed by algorithms into a playlist is a “deeply violating experience”.
